pr_title: fix(ngcc): allow deep-import warnings to be ignored
pr_body:
This commit adds a new ngcc configuration, `ignorableDeepImportMatchers`
for packages. This is a list of regular expressions matching deep imports
that can be safely ignored from that package. Deep imports that are not
ignored cause a warning to be logged.

// FW-1892

Fixes #35615
pr_comments: Here is a demo of the kind of ngcc.config.js that can now be used to fix these unwanted warnings: https://github.com/petebacondarwin/angular-issue-35615/commit/acdc35733362a2c5e01477b8874753b245c0c4ac
@petebacondarwin How do we know whether it's safe to ignore the warning or if we should actually try to fix it? Thank you!

This warning can happily be ignored if the package is not compiled by Angular (i.e. has not `...metadata.json` files) and does not depend upon packages that are compiled by Angular.
Furthermore, even if the package is compiled by Angular, ngcc will still process it but there is a chance that the order in which packages are processed might be incorrect. In this case it would most likely lead to a processing error in ngcc, a compile-time error in `ng build` (and similar) or a runtime error. If you are getting known of these, and you can see that the order in which packages are being processed is correct then it is also safe to ignore these warnings.

issue_context.title: Entry point 'xxx' contains deep imports into 'yyy'
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Is this a regression? Yes, the previous version in which this bug was not present was: 8.2.14 ### Description Multiple warnings like "Entry point 'devextreme-angular/...' contains deep imports into '/node_modules/devextreme/...'. This is probably not a problem, but may cause the compilation of entry points to be out of order." occur when building an Angular v9 project with Ivy enabled. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction [https://github.com/onebalaban/dxangular9](https://github.com/onebalaban/dxangular9) npm install ng build ## 🌍 Your Environment 

Angular CLI: 9.0.3
Node: 13.9.0
OS: win32 x64

Angular: 9.0.2
... animations, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core, forms
... language-service, platform-browser, platform-browser-dynamic
... router
Ivy Workspace: Yes

Package                           Version
-----------------------------------------------------------
@angular-devkit/architect         0.900.3
@angular-devkit/build-angular     0.900.3
@angular-devkit/build-optimizer   0.900.3
@angular-devkit/build-webpack     0.900.3
@angular-devkit/core              7.3.9
@angular-devkit/schematics        7.3.9
@angular/cli                      9.0.3
@ngtools/webpack                  9.0.3
@schematics/angular               8.3.20
@schematics/update                0.900.3
rxjs                              6.5.4
typescript                        3.7.5
webpack                           4.41.2
**Anything else relevant?** There are two packages in the project. The first one is [devextreme-angular](https://github.com/DevExpress/devextreme-angular). It is created according to Angular library requirements. The second package is **devextreme**. It is not an Angular library. The thing is that warnings are related to long paths of this second package. We think these warnings are false-positive.
comments: I'm currently with the same problem, did you found a workaround?

These are only warnings. Given that the `devextreme` package is not compiled by Angular then, as pointed out in the message: "This is probably not a problem."

It is not possible for ngcc to know whether the deep imports are going to be problematic or not, so it is reasonable to give the developer this information so that they can make a decision for themselves.

How do we remove these warnings? So many false warnings in my opinion 

> On Feb 24, 2020, at 9:41 PM, Alex Rickabaugh <notifications@github.com> wrote:
> 
> ﻿
> Closed #35615.
> 
> —
> You are receiving this because you commented.
> Reply to this email directly, view it on GitHub, or unsubscribe.
Currently this is not possible, but I will look into a way to add a configuration to ngcc to allow you to ignore deep imports for specific entry-points.
I don't think it works with local libraries - if I remember correctly ngcc.config.js expects packages to be below a node_modules directory.

But I think you could put the `ngcc.config.js` directly into the local package folder using a slightly different syntax...

```
projects/
    ngx-openlayers/  <----- lib with ol in peerDependencies
      ngcc.config.js       <----- put ngcc.config.js here
      ng-package.json
/src                 <----- demo project
```

```ts
// ngcc.config.js
module.exports = {
  ignorableDeepImportMatchers: [/ol\//]
};
```

I just tried it always does the same thing.
I put a log in `ngcc.config.js` and I don't have the impression that it is used.
Please open a new issue with a reproduction of your scenario, and I can look into it.

> Steps to silence the warning:
> 
> 1. Update to Angular 9.0.4
> 2. Create a file named 'ngcc.config.js' at your top-level project folder (see #35683)
> 
> ```
> module.exports = {
>   packages: {
>     'angular2-text-mask': {
>       ignorableDeepImportMatchers: [
>         /text-mask-core\//,
>       ]
>     },
>   },
> };
> ```
> 
> 1. Enjoy a peaceful build relieved

Thanks. That advice is helps me

To me, it kinda works. There were like 3 duplicated warnings. Now I only got 2 duplicated warnings lol.


**update**

I figured out why. 

Because I have paths mapping in tsconfig like lib: ["dist/lib"]. And I haven't rebuild the library with ngcc.config.js yet. 

2 duplicated is because of the duplicated path mappings.

```suggestion
   * A collection of regexes that match deep imports to ignore, for this project, rather than
```
This seems to be a project level configuration, not a package one?
Actually it is at the package level. You define the regexes for each package that will do the importing. This way we can isolate turning off warnings only to specific packages.
